audit.whatIsWrong: Five rows disagree with the packet, each contradicting the why beside it: win[1]='Irelia' vs whys[1] 'Level 2 stays even'; win[3]='Skill' vs whys[3] 'Levels 4-5 stay hers'; win[4]='Skill' vs whys[4] 'Level 6 swings to you'; win[5]='Irelia' vs whys[5] 'the lane evens'; win[6]='Irelia' vs whys[6] 'an even skirmish'.
audit.why: Packet chart: Skill, Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Wukong, Skill, Skill, and the irelia__wukong mirror is set to exactly that. Win rate 59.6% over 448 games — the strongest matchup in this slice, and the chart as it stands hands Irelia four rows.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs; Level 6 rating raised to 6/10 since Wukong now owns it.

audit.why: Irelia's spikes are Bladesurge resets from level 3 (10/9/8/7/6s, refreshed on a Marked target or a kill), Flawless Duet (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s), and her attack-speed passive with a first bruiser item. Vanguard's Edge is 125s at rank 1 — a long punish window. Wukong's spike is level 6.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into report[5].t and dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance appears NOWHERE on this page in either layer, and it is the ability that most directly beats Wukong. Riot's W text: 'Irelia charges a strike that deals more damage as she charges. She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Wukong's damage is physical, so a charging W blunts the entire E-Q burst the page is built around. The page instead attributes her mid-lane strength to 'passive stacks'.
audit.why: Ionian Fervor gives stacking attack speed and, at max stacks, bonus on-hit damage — real, but it does not explain why bursting her fails. The physical damage reduction on a 20/18/16/14/12s cooldown does.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance cuts the physical damage she takes while charging, so committing burst into a charging W wastes it — wait the charge out, then trade.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flawless Duet is named page-wide as the cooldown to track, with no number, and Bladesurge's reset condition is described loosely as resetting 'off minions'.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1. Bladesurge refreshes specifically if the target is Marked OR dies to it — so a Marked champion resets it just as a dying minion does, which is why denying minions alone is not enough.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit's derived flags mark Flawless Duet with 'grounding — shuts off enemy dashes', but Riot's own text for that ability says only 'damaged, stunned and Marked'.
audit.why: Per the data rules, when a derived flag contradicts Riot's description the description wins. I did not write any grounding claim into the page.
audit.corrected: No grounding claim written; recorded here instead.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay hers with the Flawless Duet stun locking your all-ins.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay hers as Defiant Dance blunts your physical burst combo.

edits.before: Even again at first item — she spikes with her passive stacks and a completed bruiser piece, but your W decoy dodges her E stun and your Q shreds her, so trade only when her Bladesurge target is gone.
edits.after: Even again at first item — her passive stacks attack speed off every spell hit, and Defiant Dance (W) cuts the PHYSICAL damage she takes while charging, so burst into a charging W does almost nothing. Wait it out.

edits.before: Stack her passive and win prolonged duels
edits.after: Charge Defiant Dance to eat your burst

edits.before: Track Irelia's Flawless Duet (Stun): Her engage CC. Decoy it. When it is down — E-Q + R her.
edits.after: Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1. Defiant Dance cuts the physical damage she takes as it charges.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Bladesurge refreshes off a Marked target or a kill — deny both.

notes: Defiant Dance was missing from both layers of this page entirely, and it is the single ability that most directly answers Wukong: it reduces the PHYSICAL damage she takes while charging, which is the whole of your E-Q burst. The page credited her mid-lane strength to 'passive stacks' instead. Also tightened Bladesurge's reset condition — the page says she resets 'off minions', but Riot's text refreshes it on a Marked target OR a kill, so a Marked champion resets it too and denying minions alone will not stop the chain. Level chart: five of seven rows disagreed with the packet and with their own whys, on the highest-win-rate matchup in my slice (59.6%); flipped to match the irelia__wukong mirror. NOT WRITTEN: the kit's derived flags tag Flawless Duet as grounding, but Riot's text for it mentions only damage, stun and Mark — flag contradicts description, so I asserted nothing about grounding.
